trails.title: Wallet foundations
trails.dek: From recorded entropy to keys, paths, scripts and destinations.

trails.title: Spending & transactions
trails.dek: How spending rules are committed, signed, timed and carried between devices.

trails.title: Signatures & spending policies
trails.dek: From one verification equation to hidden branches and shared signing.

trails.title: Privacy & coordination
trails.dek: Receiving, proving and finding payments without asking the whole network for everything.

trails.title: Network & upgrades
trails.dek: The connections between nodes, and the state machines that change their rules.

relationships.label: seed becomes keys
relationships.reason: BIP 39 derives a seed from words; BIP 32 uses seed material to begin an extended-key tree.

relationships.label: give the tree a layout
relationships.reason: BIP 32 supplies derivation; wallet-path BIPs assign meanings to particular branches and script families.

relationships.label: paths inside expressions
relationships.reason: Descriptors combine key origins, derivation paths and script templates into a wallet-readable expression.

relationships.label: scripts become destinations
relationships.reason: Descriptors describe the scripts a wallet watches; addresses encode particular output destinations for senders.

relationships.label: v1 uses Bech32m
relationships.reason: Taproot outputs use witness version 1; the address chapter explains the Bech32m rule their addresses require.

relationships.label: destinations become instructions
relationships.reason: Payment URIs wrap an address and add amounts, metadata and alternative payment methods. The address and the instruction are different validity questions.

relationships.label: sp becomes a query key
relationships.reason: BIP 321 names sp for BIP 352 Silent Payment addresses, including forms with no on-chain fallback.

relationships.label: compatibility wrapper
relationships.reason: P2SH can wrap SegWit programs, separating the outer hash commitment from the witness program inside.

relationships.label: toward a signed transaction
relationships.reason: PSBT carries a transaction and signing information; SegWit explains the serialization and witness a completed spend can produce.

relationships.label: extend the signing package
relationships.reason: PSBTv2 changes construction, while Taproot and MuSig2 fields add the metadata modern signing rounds need.

relationships.label: rounds inside a PSBT
relationships.reason: BIP 373 carries MuSig2 participants, public nonces and partial signatures inside the PSBT package introduced by the earlier chapters.

relationships.label: one sequence field, two jobs
relationships.reason: BIP 68 uses nSequence for relative locks; BIP 125 uses it for replaceability signaling. Consensus locktimes and mempool replacement policy must stay separate.

relationships.label: locks inside scripts
relationships.reason: Absolute and relative lock opcodes can appear inside the Taproot scripts that Tapscript executes.

relationships.label: verify the key path
relationships.reason: Taproot key-path spends rely on the BIP 340 Schnorr signature rules.

relationships.label: run the revealed leaf
relationships.reason: Taproot commits to and reveals a script leaf; Tapscript supplies the rules for executing it.

relationships.label: one ordinary signature
relationships.reason: MuSig2 produces a signature that a BIP 340 verifier checks like a single-signer Schnorr signature.

relationships.label: fresh Taproot outputs
relationships.reason: Silent Payments let senders derive fresh Taproot outputs from a reusable address and transaction data.

relationships.label: virtual transactions
relationships.reason: BIP 322 builds virtual transactions and verifies script and witness rules; SegWit explains the transaction pieces those proofs reuse.

relationships.label: wtxid enters relay
relationships.reason: Compact Block Relay v2 computes six-byte short IDs from wtxid rather than txid, linking relay to the SegWit serialization model.

relationships.label: compact relay on the wire
relationships.reason: Compact block messages travel over peer connections; v2 transport changes their encryption, not their reconstruction rules.

relationships.label: addresses before encryption
relationships.reason: Addr v2 tells peers where to connect; v2 transport then protects the connection, not the endpoint’s identity or reachability.

relationships.label: filters on the wire
relationships.reason: Compact filters are queried from peers; v2 transport changes the connection carrying those messages, not the filter rules.

relationships.label: activation context
relationships.reason: Version bits explains deployment state machines; Taproot is the upgrade whose activation context readers can investigate next.
